purpose: Keep one active Continuity protocol while preserving business history and explicit migration edges, with technical and user-facing version namespaces kept distinct.

versioning.principle: Do not create a new protocol version for every internal improvement.

git_commit.rule: Keep Git as the engineering source of truth. A human revision never replaces or reinterprets the commit SHA.

protocol.rule: Protocol versions describe compatibility semantics, not chronological submissions.

durable_state_version.source: authoritative manifest_version or owner-equivalent durable version
durable_state_version.rule: This version remains the concurrency/state sequence used by the task or owner. It may advance for durable control-state transitions as well as user-visible content progress; gaps are valid and must not be renumbered.

controller_revision.rule: Controller revision is internal to one maintenance run and is not a repository or product version.

human_revision.date_source: calendar date from the authoritative persisted timestamp exactly as encoded
human_revision.ordering_rule: rN orders revisions within one scope; date is calendar context only
human_revision.svn_semantics_borrowed: human-friendly monotonic revision concept only; do not emulate SVN's centralized repository-global counter across Git repositories
human_revision.cross_owner_rule: Each owner/task revision stream uses its own existing monotonic durable version and stable scope code. Numbers from different scopes are not globally comparable.
human_revision.adoption_precondition: A suitable monotonic durable version must already exist for the intended identity lifetime. If not, do not invent a display-only counter; fix the owner version model separately.

migration_invariants: Preserve task_id, owner business state, current_stage, next_action, business artifacts and valid active lease unless the business owner itself requires a migration.
Protocol migration may add observability, metadata and compatibility fields without replaying completed business work.
Unknown or unsupported old state fails closed instead of being guessed from chat memory.
Historical paused/archived tasks may be migrated lazily when explicitly resumed; they do not need eager writes merely because the protocol changed.
Human revision presentation changes must not rewrite Git history, reset durable owner/task versions, force protocol migration, or persist a duplicate derived revision label.
